title: LINE-1 insertion intermediates recombine with one another or with DNA breaks to form genome rearrangements
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76308-7

LINE-1 retrotransposition is associated with genome instability in cancers, yet the mechanisms are not fully understood. Here, the authors combine recombination reporter assays with long-read sequencing to show that retrotransposition intermediates can recombine with one another or with DNA breaks to produce chromosomal rearrangements.

title: The transcription factor C/EBPβ promotes hyperglycemia-elicited glycolysis and liver cancer progression
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76209-9

High blood sugar in diabetes is linked to faster cancer growth, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor C/EBPβ is activated by high glucose to enhance glycolysis and HRAS-driven proliferation, promoting liver cancer progression and revealing a potential therapeutic target.

title: Where the river turns old: urbanized deltas imprint a fossil signature on black carbon exported to the ocean
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76202-2

Whether fossil black carbon (BC) biases the 14C age of riverine BC is unclear. This study shows urbanized deltas add fossil BC, making BC 14C age appear much older and underscoring the need for landuse context when estimating BC residence time on land.

title: Corisin induces proteostasis stress to drive epithelial injury and pulmonary fibrosis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76162-7

Here, the authors establish the naturally occurring microbiota-derived Corisin as a potent driver of lung injury and fibrosis, revealing a previously unrecognized microbial pathway that disrupts epithelial cell function and promotes pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Ruxolitinib prevents irreversible autoimmune endocrinopathies in APECED
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76285-x

APECED is a monogenic autoimmune disorder resulting from deleterious variants in the Autoimmune Regulator gene. Here, the authors report the cases of two patients with APECED in whom early intervention with the JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib prevented endocrine autoimmunity.

title: A molecular velcro self-healing cement
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76061-x

A “molecular Velcro” cement with trace amounts of polymer rapidly heals cracks through reversible molecular interactions and pore-scale transport, restoring strength across damage cycles and offering a scalable path to longer-lasting concrete.

title: All-small-molecule Hydrogels for Safe and Efficient Photoprotection
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75884-y

Commercial sunscreens rely on organic and inorganic UV filters that may generate ROS and induce phototoxicity, raising safety concerns. Encapsulation strategies mitigate transdermal penetration but add formulation complexity and cost. Here, the authors introduce carrier-free, all-small-molecule hydrogels formed via one-pot integration of natural polyphenols and aminoglycosides. These materials provide effective UV protection, antioxidant and antibacterial activity, good biosafety, and limited skin penetration, offering a promising, simpler alternative to conventional sunscreens.

title: A massively parallel CRISPR-based screening platform for modifiers of neuronal depolarization
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75882-0

We currently lack scalable approaches to systematically reveal the genetic underpinnings of neuronal function in health and disease. Here, the authors develop a platform to uncover genes affecting neuronal excitability in scalable CRISPR screens.
